name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ALCOHOLS_PHENOLS_AND_ETHERS_MATCHING_Q01 - Common and IUPAC names of hydroxybenzenes

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Common Name) List II (IUPAC Name)
(A) Catechol (I) Benzene-1,3-diol
(B) Resorcinol (II) Benzene-1,4-diol
(C) Hydroquinone (III) Propane-1,2,3-triol
(D) Glycerol (IV) Benzene-1,2-diol

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Nomenclature of Catechol
Catechol is a dihydroxybenzene containing two hydroxyl groups attached to adjacent carbon atoms of the benzene ring. Its systematic IUPAC name is benzene-1,2-diol.

Step 2: Nomenclature of Resorcinol
Resorcinol contains two hydroxyl groups positioned at carbon-1 and carbon-3 of the benzene ring. Its systematic IUPAC name is benzene-1,3-diol.

Step 3: Nomenclature of Hydroquinone
Hydroquinone (also known as quinol) has two hydroxyl groups situated at opposite carbon atoms (positions 1 and 4) of the benzene ring. Its systematic IUPAC name is benzene-1,4-diol.

Step 4: Nomenclature of Glycerol
Glycerol is a trihydric alcohol featuring three hydroxyl groups attached to a three-carbon aliphatic chain. Its systematic IUPAC name is propane-1,2,3-triol.

Conclusion:
Catechol pairs with benzene-1,2-diol; Resorcinol pairs with benzene-1,3-diol; Hydroquinone pairs with benzene-1,4-diol; and Glycerol pairs with propane-1,2,3-triol.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ALCOHOLS_PHENOLS_AND_ETHERS_MATCHING_Q02 - Reagents for industrial alcohols and phenol conversions

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Chemical Conversion / Process) List II (Reagent / Catalyst Involved)
(A) Catalytic hydrogenation of carbon monoxide to methanol (I) Zinc dust and heat
(B) Fermentation of glucose to ethanol (II) Acetic anhydride in the presence of acid
(C) Reduction of phenol to benzene (III) \(\mathrm{ZnO}-\mathrm{Cr}_2\mathrm{O}_3\) catalyst at \(200\text{--}300\text{ atm}\) and \(573\text{--}673\text{ K}\)
(D) Acetylation of salicylic acid to aspirin (IV) Zymase enzyme

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Methanol Production
Methanol is commercially manufactured by the catalytic hydrogenation of carbon monoxide in the presence of a \(\mathrm{ZnO}-\mathrm{Cr}_2\mathrm{O}_3\) catalyst at high pressure (\(200\text{--}300\text{ atm}\)) and elevated temperature (\(573\text{--}673\text{ K}\)).

Step 2: Ethanol Fermentation
During alcoholic fermentation, glucose and fructose are converted into ethanol and carbon dioxide under the catalytic action of the enzyme zymase, which is naturally present in yeast.

Step 3: Reduction of Phenol
Heating phenol directly with zinc dust removes the oxygen atom via reduction, producing benzene and zinc oxide.

Step 4: Aspirin Synthesis
The acetylation of salicylic acid (2-hydroxybenzoic acid) using acetic anhydride in the presence of an acid catalyst introduces an acetyl group onto the phenolic hydroxyl group, yielding acetylsalicylic acid (aspirin).

Conclusion:
Catalytic hydrogenation of carbon monoxide to methanol pairs with the zinc oxide-chromium oxide catalyst at 200 to 300 atmospheres and 573 to 673 kelvin; Fermentation of glucose to ethanol pairs with zymase enzyme; Reduction of phenol to benzene pairs with zinc dust and heat; and Acetylation of salicylic acid to aspirin pairs with acetic anhydride in the presence of acid.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ALCOHOLS_PHENOLS_AND_ETHERS_MATCHING_Q03 - Reactions for the laboratory preparation of phenol

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Starting Material) List II (Method / Reagents for Preparing Phenol)
(A) Chlorobenzene (I) Sulphonation with oleum, then heating with molten \(\mathrm{NaOH}\), followed by acidification
(B) Benzene (II) Diazotisation with \(\mathrm{NaNO}_2 + \mathrm{HCl}\) at \(273\text{--}278\text{ K}\), followed by warming with water
(C) Aniline (III) Aerial oxidation to cumene hydroperoxide, followed by hydrolysis with dilute acid
(D) Cumene (IV) Fusion with \(\mathrm{NaOH}\) at \(623\text{ K}\) and \(300\text{ atm}\), followed by acidification

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conversion of Chlorobenzene
Chlorobenzene is fused with sodium hydroxide under drastic conditions (temperature of \(623\text{ K}\) and pressure of \(300\text{ atm}\)) to produce sodium phenoxide, which upon acidification with hydrochloric acid yields phenol (Dow's process).

Step 2: Conversion of Benzene
Benzene is sulphonated with oleum to form benzenesulphonic acid. Heating benzenesulphonic acid with molten sodium hydroxide converts it to sodium phenoxide, which produces phenol upon acidification.

Step 3: Conversion of Aniline
Aniline undergoes diazotisation when treated with nitrous acid (from sodium nitrite and hydrochloric acid) at \(273\text{--}278\text{ K}\) to yield benzenediazonium chloride, which readily hydrolyses to phenol upon warming with water.

Step 4: Conversion of Cumene
Cumene (isopropylbenzene) is oxidised by atmospheric oxygen to cumene hydroperoxide, which upon treatment with dilute acid undergoes rearrangement to yield phenol along with acetone as a valuable by-product.

Conclusion:
Chlorobenzene pairs with fusion with sodium hydroxide at 623 kelvin and 300 atmospheres followed by acidification; Benzene pairs with sulphonation with oleum, then heating with molten sodium hydroxide, followed by acidification; Aniline pairs with diazotisation with sodium nitrite and hydrochloric acid at 273 to 278 kelvin followed by warming with water; and Cumene pairs with aerial oxidation to cumene hydroperoxide followed by dilute acid hydrolysis.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ALCOHOLS_PHENOLS_AND_ETHERS_MATCHING_Q04 - Major products of distinctive reactions of phenol

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Reaction of Phenol) List II (Major Organic Product)
(A) Kolbe's reaction (I) Salicylaldehyde
(B) Reimer-Tiemann reaction (II) 2,4,6-Tribromophenol
(C) Reaction with bromine water (III) Benzoquinone
(D) Oxidation with acidified sodium dichromate (IV) 2-Hydroxybenzoic acid

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Product of Kolbe's Reaction
In Kolbe's reaction, sodium phenoxide reacts with carbon dioxide under pressure followed by acidification, introducing a carboxyl group ortho to the phenolic hydroxyl group to produce 2-hydroxybenzoic acid (salicylic acid).

Step 2: Product of Reimer-Tiemann Reaction
In the Reimer-Tiemann reaction, treating phenol with chloroform in the presence of aqueous sodium hydroxide introduces an aldehyde group ortho to the hydroxyl group, yielding salicylaldehyde.

Step 3: Product with Bromine Water
Due to the strong activation of the aromatic ring by the hydroxyl group, treating phenol with bromine water results in polyhalogenation at all activated positions (ortho and para), giving 2,4,6-tribromophenol as a white precipitate.

Step 4: Product of Oxidation with Dichromate
Oxidation of phenol with acidified sodium dichromate (chromic acid) leads to conjugated diketone formation, producing benzoquinone.

Conclusion:
Kolbe's reaction pairs with 2-hydroxybenzoic acid (salicylic acid); Reimer-Tiemann reaction pairs with salicylaldehyde; Reaction of phenol with bromine water pairs with 2,4,6-tribromophenol; and Oxidation of phenol with acidified sodium dichromate pairs with benzoquinone.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ALCOHOLS_PHENOLS_AND_ETHERS_MATCHING_Q05 - Oxidation and dehydrogenation products of aliphatic alcohols

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Substrate and Reaction Conditions) List II (Major Product)
(A) \(\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{OH} + \mathrm{PCC}\) (I) Propanone
(B) Propan-2-ol \(+ \mathrm{CrO}_3\) (II) 2-Methylpropene
(C) Ethanol \(+ \text{acidified }\mathrm{KMnO}_4\) (III) \(\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CHO}\)
(D) 2-Methylpropan-2-ol \(+ \mathrm{Cu}\text{ at }573\text{ K}\) (IV) Ethanoic acid

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Oxidation with PCC
Pyridinium chlorochromate (PCC) is a selective reagent that oxidises primary alcohols to aldehydes without affecting carbon-carbon double bonds. Thus, but-2-en-1-ol is oxidised directly to but-2-enal (\(\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CHO}\)).

Step 2: Oxidation of Secondary Alcohol with Chromic Anhydride
Secondary alcohols undergo oxidation with chromic anhydride (\(\mathrm{CrO}_3\)) in anhydrous conditions to form ketones. Propan-2-ol is converted into propanone.

Step 3: Oxidation with Acidified Permanganate
Potassium permanganate in acidic medium is a strong oxidising agent that oxidises primary alcohols directly to carboxylic acids. Ethanol is completely oxidised to ethanoic acid.

Step 4: Dehydration over Heated Copper
Tertiary alcohols do not possess alpha hydrogen atoms and resist dehydrogenation; instead, passing 2-methylpropan-2-ol vapours over heated copper at \(573\text{ K}\) causes catalytic dehydration to yield 2-methylpropene.

Conclusion:
But-2-en-1-ol with pyridinium chlorochromate pairs with but-2-enal; Propan-2-ol with chromic anhydride pairs with propanone; Ethanol with acidified potassium permanganate pairs with ethanoic acid; and 2-Methylpropan-2-ol over copper at 573 kelvin pairs with 2-methylpropene.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ALCOHOLS_PHENOLS_AND_ETHERS_MATCHING_Q06 - Bond lengths and angles of oxygen compounds

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Structural Feature) List II (Experimental Value)
(A) \(\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{O}\) bond length in phenol (I) \(142\text{ pm}\)
(B) \(\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{O}\) bond length in methanol (II) \(108.9^\circ\)
(C) \(\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{C}\) bond angle in methoxymethane (III) \(136\text{ pm}\)
(D) \(\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{H}\) bond angle in methanol (IV) \(111.7^\circ\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Bond Length in Phenol
In phenol, conjugation of the unshared electron pair of oxygen with the aromatic ring imparts partial double-bond character, and oxygen is bonded to an \(sp^2\) hybridized carbon, shortening the \(\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{O}\) bond length to \(136\text{ pm}\).

Step 2: Bond Length in Methanol
In methanol, oxygen is bonded to an \(sp^3\) hybridized carbon with a single sigma bond and no resonance shortening, giving a \(\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{O}\) bond length of \(142\text{ pm}\).

Step 3: Bond Angle in Methoxymethane
In methoxymethane (dimethyl ether), steric repulsion between the two bulky methyl groups expands the \(\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{C}\) angle beyond the regular tetrahedral geometry to \(111.7^\circ\).

Step 4: Bond Angle in Methanol
In methanol, repulsion between the two unshared lone pairs on the oxygen atom compresses the \(\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{H}\) angle slightly below the tetrahedral value (\(109.5^\circ\)) to \(108.9^\circ\).

Conclusion:
Carbon-oxygen bond length in phenol pairs with 136 picometres; Carbon-oxygen bond length in methanol pairs with 142 picometres; Carbon-oxygen-carbon bond angle in methoxymethane pairs with 111.7 degrees; and Carbon-oxygen-hydrogen bond angle in methanol pairs with 108.9 degrees.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ALCOHOLS_PHENOLS_AND_ETHERS_MATCHING_Q07 - Structural classification of allylic and benzylic alcohols

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Alcohol Structure) List II (Structural Classification)
(A) \(\mathrm{CH}_2=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{OH}\) (I) Vinylic alcohol
(B) \(\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5-\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{OH}\) (II) Secondary aliphatic alcohol
(C) \(\mathrm{CH}_2=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{OH}\) (III) Primary allylic alcohol
(D) \(\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{OH})-\mathrm{CH}_3\) (IV) Primary benzylic alcohol

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Classification of Prop-2-en-1-ol
In prop-2-en-1-ol (\(\mathrm{CH}_2=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{OH}\)), the hydroxyl group is bonded to an \(sp^3\) hybridised carbon directly adjacent to a carbon-carbon double bond, with only one carbon attached to this carbinol centre; hence it is a primary allylic alcohol.

Step 2: Classification of Phenylmethanol
In phenylmethanol (benzyl alcohol, \(\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5-\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{OH}\)), the hydroxyl group is attached to an \(sp^3\) hybridised carbon adjacent to an aromatic benzene ring, classifying it as a primary benzylic alcohol.

Step 3: Classification of Ethenol
In ethenol (\(\mathrm{CH}_2=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{OH}\)), the hydroxyl group is directly attached to a carbon forming a carbon-carbon double bond (\(sp^2\) hybridised carbon), which defines a vinylic alcohol.

Step 4: Classification of Propan-2-ol
In propan-2-ol (\(\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{OH})-\mathrm{CH}_3\)), the hydroxyl-bearing carbon is an \(sp^3\) aliphatic carbon bonded to two alkyl groups and one hydrogen atom, designating it as a secondary aliphatic alcohol.

Conclusion:
Prop-2-en-1-ol pairs with primary allylic alcohol; Benzyl alcohol pairs with primary benzylic alcohol; Ethenol pairs with vinylic alcohol; and Propan-2-ol pairs with secondary aliphatic alcohol.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ALCOHOLS_PHENOLS_AND_ETHERS_MATCHING_Q08 - Products of acidic cleavage of unsymmetrical ethers

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Ether Subjected to Cleavage with 1 Equivalent of \(\mathrm{HI}\)) List II (Pair of Products Formed)
(A) \(\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5-\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{CH}_3\) (I) \((\mathrm{CH}_3)_3\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{I} + \mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{OH}\)
(B) \((\mathrm{CH}_3)_3\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{CH}_3\) (II) \(\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{OH} + \mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{I}\)
(C) \(\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{CH}_3\) (III) \(\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{I} + \mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{OH}\)
(D) \(\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{CH}_3\) (IV) \(\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{I} + \mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{OH}\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Cleavage of Anisole
In methyl phenyl ether (anisole), the oxygen atom is conjugated with the aromatic ring, giving the phenylic \(\mathrm{C}_{sp^2}-\mathrm{O}\) bond partial double-bond character. Nucleophilic attack by iodide ion occurs selectively at the weaker aliphatic methyl group via an \(\mathrm{S_N2}\) pathway, producing phenol and methyl iodide.

Step 2: Cleavage of tert-Butyl Methyl Ether
When one alkyl group is tertiary, protonation of ether is followed by unimolecular departure of the leaving group (methanol) via an \(\mathrm{S_N1}\) mechanism because a highly stable tertiary carbocation \([(\mathrm{CH}_3)_3\mathrm{C}^+]\) is generated. Subsequent addition of iodide yields tert-butyl iodide and methanol.

Step 3: Cleavage of Benzyl Ethyl Ether
In benzyl ethyl ether, departure of the leaving group ethanol leads to the formation of a resonance-stabilised benzylic carbocation (or displacement occurs preferentially at the benzylic carbon due to high benzylic reactivity), giving benzyl iodide and ethanol as products.

Step 4: Cleavage of Methyl n-Propyl Ether
In dialkyl ethers containing primary alkyl groups, cleavage proceeds predominantly through an \(\mathrm{S_N2}\) mechanism where iodide attacks the sterically less hindered methyl carbon, producing methyl iodide and propan-1-ol.

Conclusion:
Anisole pairs with phenol and methyl iodide; tert-Butyl methyl ether pairs with tert-butyl iodide and methanol; Benzyl ethyl ether pairs with benzyl iodide and ethanol; and Methyl n-propyl ether pairs with methyl iodide and propan-1-ol.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ALCOHOLS_PHENOLS_AND_ETHERS_MATCHING_Q09 - Acid strength and pKa values of phenols

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Phenolic Compound) List II (\(\mathrm{pK_a}\) Value at \(298\text{ K}\))
(A) 4-Nitrophenol (I) \(10.2\)
(B) 3-Nitrophenol (II) \(7.1\)
(C) Phenol (III) \(8.3\)
(D) 4-Methylphenol (IV) \(10.0\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Acidity of 4-Nitrophenol
At the para position, the strongly electron-withdrawing nitro group stabilizes the phenoxide ion through combined inductive (\(-I\)) and powerful resonance (\(-R\)) delocalisation of negative charge. This greatly enhances acidity, corresponding to the lowest \(\mathrm{pK_a}\) value of \(7.1\).

Step 2: Acidity of 3-Nitrophenol
At the meta position, resonance delocalisation of the negative charge onto the nitro group is not possible, so stabilization of the phenoxide ion occurs only through the inductive (\(-I\)) effect. Consequently, it is less acidic than the para isomer but more acidic than unsubstituted phenol, having a \(\mathrm{pK_a}\) of \(8.3\).

Step 3: Acidity of Phenol
Unsubstituted phenol has no substituent modifying the ring electron density. Resonance stabilization of the phenoxide ion gives it a baseline \(\mathrm{pK_a}\) value of \(10.0\).

Step 4: Acidity of 4-Methylphenol
In 4-methylphenol (para-cresol), the methyl group is electron-releasing via inductive effect (\(+I\)) and hyperconjugation. This destabilises the phenoxide ion and reduces acidity compared to phenol, resulting in a higher \(\mathrm{pK_a}\) of \(10.2\).

Conclusion:
4-Nitrophenol pairs with a pKa of 7.1; 3-Nitrophenol pairs with a pKa of 8.3; Phenol pairs with a pKa of 10.0; and 4-Methylphenol pairs with a pKa of 10.2.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ALCOHOLS_PHENOLS_AND_ETHERS_MATCHING_Q10 - Dehydration conditions and mechanisms of aliphatic alcohols

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Reaction Conditions) List II (Reaction Outcome / Major Product)
(A) \(\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{OH}\) with conc. \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{SO}_4\) at \(443\text{ K}\) (I) 2-Methylpropene via tertiary carbocation intermediate
(B) \(\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{OH})-\mathrm{CH}_3\) with \(85\%\ \mathrm{H}_3\mathrm{PO}_4\) at \(440\text{ K}\) (II) Propene via secondary carbocation intermediate
(C) \((\mathrm{CH}_3)_3\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{OH}\) with \(20\%\ \mathrm{H}_3\mathrm{PO}_4\) at \(358\text{ K}\) (III) Ethoxyethane via bimolecular nucleophilic substitution
(D) \(\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{OH}\) with conc. \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{SO}_4\) at \(413\text{ K}\) (IV) Ethene via elimination involving carbocation intermediate

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: High-Temperature Dehydration of Ethanol
Heating ethanol with concentrated sulphuric acid at \(443\text{ K}\) favours elimination over substitution. Protonation of alcohol is followed by rate-determining loss of water to form a carbocation, which then loses a proton to yield ethene.

Step 2: Dehydration of Secondary Alcohol
Dehydration of secondary alcohols proceeds under milder conditions than primary alcohols due to greater stability of secondary carbocations. Heating propan-2-ol with \(85\%\) phosphoric acid at \(440\text{ K}\) produces propene.

Step 3: Dehydration of Tertiary Alcohol
Tertiary carbocations possess high stability and form readily; therefore, 2-methylpropan-2-ol dehydrates under very mild conditions (\(20\%\) phosphoric acid at \(358\text{ K}\)) to yield 2-methylpropene.

Step 4: Low-Temperature Dehydration of Ethanol
When ethanol is heated with concentrated sulphuric acid at the lower temperature of \(413\text{ K}\), bimolecular nucleophilic substitution (\(\mathrm{S_N2}\)) predominates, in which an unprotonated ethanol molecule attacks the protonated alcohol to yield ethoxyethane (diethyl ether).

Conclusion:
Ethanol heated with concentrated sulphuric acid at 443 kelvin pairs with ethene via elimination involving a carbocation intermediate; Propan-2-ol heated with 85% phosphoric acid at 440 kelvin pairs with propene via a secondary carbocation intermediate; 2-Methylpropan-2-ol heated with 20% phosphoric acid at 358 kelvin pairs with 2-methylpropene via a tertiary carbocation intermediate; and Ethanol heated with concentrated sulphuric acid at 413 kelvin pairs with ethoxyethane via bimolecular nucleophilic substitution.
